name: bayes-group-site
summary: Static marketing site for The Bayes Group built with Vite + React + TypeScript + react-router and plain CSS design tokens. All copy and logic live in plain TypeScript modules that Jest tests without rendering: site and nav config, page titles, home, services, courses and about content, course filtering, contact form validation and submit, and theme tokens with a contrast helper. React pages render from these modules.
steps: Set up package.json (private, "type": "module"). Scripts: "dev": "vite", "build": "tsc -b && vite build" (or "vite build"; it must produce dist/index.html) and "test": "jest". Dependencies: react, react-dom, react-router-dom (v6 or v7). devDependencies: vite, @vitejs/plugin-react, typescript, @types/react, @types/react-dom, jest, ts-jest, @types/jest, @types/node. No preinstall, postinstall or prepare scripts.

Create jest.config.cjs: testEnvironment 'node', testMatch ['**/__tests__/**/*.test.ts'], and a transform of '^.+\\.tsx?$' to ['ts-jest', { tsconfig: { module: 'commonjs', moduleResolution: 'node', esModuleInterop: true, jsx: 'react-jsx', target: 'ES2020', strict: true, isolatedModules: true } }]. Modules under src/content, src/lib/contactForm.ts, src/lib/contrast.ts and src/theme/tokens.ts must be plain TS: no React, no CSS imports, no import.meta.

index.html: lang="en", meta viewport, title 'The Bayes Group | Evidence-driven AI', and only the local module script /src/main.tsx. It has no external <script src="http..."> and no <link href="http..."> (no font or image CDNs, no analytics).

src/theme/tokens.ts: export const THEME = { navy: '#0B1F3A', white: '#FFFFFF', accent: '#1F8A8A', accentText: <a darker teal hex with contrast of at least 4.5 on white, e.g. '#17696A'>, text: <body text hex>, mutedText: <hex> }. All values are 6-digit hex. text, mutedText and accentText must each have a contrast of at least 4.5:1 on white.

src/styles/theme.css: a :root block defining CSS custom properties, including --color-navy: #0B1F3A, --color-accent: #1F8A8A, --color-white, --font-serif (a system serif stack ending in serif, e.g. Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif) and --font-sans (a system stack ending in sans-serif). No @import of remote URLs. global.css: headings use var(--font-serif) and body uses var(--font-sans). Use visible :focus-visible outlines. Add html, body { overflow-x: hidden } plus max-width:100% for media. Use a mobile breakpoint (<= 768px) where the nav collapses behind a 'Menu' button with aria-expanded and aria-controls.
src/lib/contrast.ts: export function contrastRatio(hexA: string, hexB: string): number, using the WCAG 2 relative-luminance formula. It accepts '#RRGGBB' case-insensitively and is symmetric.

src/content/site.ts: export SITE_NAME = 'The Bayes Group', TAGLINE = 'Evidence-driven AI, built for your business.', FOOTER_LINE = 'AI enablement, training and custom development.', COPYRIGHT = '© 2026 The Bayes Group', CONTACT_EMAIL = 'hello@thebayesgroup.com', NAV_LINKS = [{label:'Services',to:'/services'},{label:'Training',to:'/training'},{label:'About',to:'/about'},{label:'Contact',to:'/contact'}] and CTA = {label:'Book a consultation', to:'/contact'}. Also export PAGE_TITLES = { home: 'The Bayes Group | Evidence-driven AI', services: 'Services | The Bayes Group', training: 'Training | The Bayes Group', about: 'About | The Bayes Group', contact: 'Contact | The Bayes Group', notFound: 'Page not found | The Bayes Group' } and getPageTitle(pathname: string): string. getPageTitle maps '/', '/services', '/training', '/about' and '/contact' (ignoring a trailing slash, query and hash) to those titles, and any other path to PAGE_TITLES.notFound. Pages set document.title via a useDocumentTitle hook in src/lib/useDocumentTitle.ts.

src/content/home.ts: export HERO = { title: 'Evidence-driven AI, built for your business.', valueProp: <one sentence>, primary: {label:'Book a consultation', to:'/contact'}, secondary: {label:'Explore services', to:'/services'} }. PILLARS = [{title:'AI Enablement', description, href:'/services#enablement'}, {title:'Training', description, href:'/services#training'}, {title:'Custom Development', description, href:'/services#custom-development'}]; each description has 2-3 sentences. STEPS = [{title:'Assess', description}, {title:'Design', ...}, {title:'Build', ...}, {title:'Enable', ...}]. WHY_POINTS: 4 items of {title, description}, covering credentialed data scientists, hands-on builders, vendor-neutral advice and knowledge transfer. CTA_BAND = { heading: 'Ready to put AI to work?', button: {label:'Book a consultation', to:'/contact'} }.

src/content/services.ts: export type ServiceItem = {name, description} and SERVICE_SECTIONS: Array<{id, title, intro, items: ServiceItem[], typicalEngagement: string}>. The sections are, in order: id 'enablement' (title 'AI Enablement') with items 'AI readiness assessment', 'Use-case discovery and prioritization', 'AI strategy and roadmap', 'AI governance and responsible-AI policy'; id 'training' (title 'Training') with items 'Executive AI briefings', 'Hands-on team workshops', 'Deep-learning bootcamps for technical teams', 'Custom curricula'; id 'custom-development' (title 'Custom Development') with items 'LLM and retrieval-augmented (RAG) applications', 'AI agents and workflow automation', 'Predictive models and ML pipelines', 'Deep-learning solutions', 'Integration with existing systems'. Each item has a non-empty one-sentence description. typicalEngagement is a short duration like '2 to 6 weeks', rendered as 'Typical engagement: 2 to 6 weeks'. ServicesPage renders <section id={id}> for each section.

src/content/courses.ts: export AUDIENCES = ['Executives','Managers','Technical teams'] as const, FORMATS = ['Half-day briefing','1-day workshop','Multi-week bootcamp'] as const, COURSE_FILTERS = ['All','Executives','Managers','Technical teams'] as const, and COURSES: Array<{id, title, audience, format, duration, learn: string[]}>. There are at least 6 courses with unique ids, every audience is covered, and each learn list has exactly 3 items. Export filterCourses(courses, filter) returning a new array: all courses for 'All', otherwise only those whose audience === filter. It never mutates its input. TrainingPage keeps the filter in state (initially 'All'), renders the 4 filter buttons with aria-pressed and a visible selected style, and lists filterCourses(COURSES, filter).

src/content/about.ts: export MISSION (a paragraph) and WHY_BAYES (a paragraph mentioning Bayesian reasoning and updating beliefs as evidence arrives). FOUNDERS: 2 items of { name: 'Founder Name', role: 'Co-founder & Principal Data Scientist', credentials: string[] (non-empty), bio: string, placeholder: true }. The page visibly labels them as placeholder content to be replaced. VALUES: [{title:'Evidence over hype'},{title:'Build to transfer'},{title:'Vendor-neutral'},{title:'Responsible by design'}], each with a description.

src/lib/contactForm.ts: export type ContactValues = {name, email, company, topic, message} (all strings). Export EMPTY_CONTACT_FORM (all ''), HELP_OPTIONS = ['AI Enablement','Training','Custom Development','Not sure yet'], ERROR_MESSAGES = {name:'Please enter your name.', email:'Please enter a valid email address.', message:'Please enter a message.'}, SUCCESS_MESSAGE = "Thanks, we'll be in touch within one business day." (ASCII apostrophe), isValidEmail(s) (trims; requires local@domain.tld with no spaces), validateContact(values) returning an object with only the invalid keys among name/email/message mapped to their ERROR_MESSAGES (whitespace-only counts as empty), and submitContact(values). submitContact makes no network request and returns { ok: true, message: SUCCESS_MESSAGE, values: { ...EMPTY_CONTACT_FORM } } when valid, or { ok: false, errors, values } (the values unchanged) otherwise. ContactPage uses these: labelled fields Name, Email, Company, 'What can we help with?' (select) and Message, a 'Send message' button, errors shown next to fields with aria-describedby/aria-invalid, noValidate on the form, and the email hello@thebayesgroup.com as a mailto link.

Components: Wordmark (inline SVG bell curve plus the text 'The Bayes Group', with an aria-label), Header (<header> with a Link to / around the wordmark, <nav aria-label='Main'> with NAV_LINKS, the CTA button, and a mobile 'Menu' toggle button with aria-expanded), Footer (<footer> with the wordmark, FOOTER_LINE, NAV_LINKS and COPYRIGHT), and Layout (Header, <main id='main'>, Footer, plus a skip link). App.tsx uses BrowserRouter with routes /, /services, /training, /about, /contact and * (NotFoundPage: h1 'Page not found' and a Link to '/'). Each page has exactly one h1: Home 'Evidence-driven AI, built for your business.', 'Services', 'Training', 'About', 'Book a consultation', 'Page not found'. Hash links (/services#training) scroll to the section on load.

Add devDependencies jest-environment-jsdom (same major version as jest), @testing-library/react, @testing-library/dom and @testing-library/user-event. Rendering acceptance tests opt into jsdom with a '@jest-environment jsdom' docblock; the default testEnvironment stays 'node'.

In jest.config.cjs add moduleNameMapper { '\\.css$': '<rootDir>/test/styleMock.cjs' } and create test/styleMock.cjs containing module.exports = {}; so components and pages that import CSS can be required in Jest.

src/App.tsx: export a named component AppRoutes that renders the <Routes> (Layout with Header, <main>, Footer, and the routes /, /services, /training, /about, /contact and * for NotFoundPage) without a Router, and export App (default and named) as <BrowserRouter><AppRoutes/></BrowserRouter>. App.tsx, src/components/* and src/pages/* must not use import.meta, so they load under ts-jest (commonjs) inside a MemoryRouter.

acceptance_files.test_acceptance.py:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Runs the app's acceptance tests: the Jest files in __tests__/acceptance/. Generated by the pipeline; the tests
themselves are locked files written by the planner. ACCEPTANCE_MILESTONE=N runs only the tests of milestones 1..N."""
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
os.chdir(here)
if not os.path.isdir("node_modules"):
    lock = os.path.exists("package-lock.json")
    subprocess.run(["npm", "ci" if lock else "install", "--include=dev", "--no-audit", "--no-fund"], check=False, timeout=1500)
cmd = ["npx", "jest", "--ci", "__tests__/acceptance"]
m = os.environ.get("ACCEPTANCE_MILESTONE", "")
if m.isdigit():
    cmd += ["-t", "^(" + "|".join("M%d" % i for i in range(1, int(m) + 1)) + "): "]
# The app's own test script may add node flags (e.g. --experimental-vm-modules): use the same ones.
try:
    script = json.load(open("package.json")).get("scripts", {}).get("test", "")
except (OSError, ValueError):
    script = ""
env = dict(os.environ)
if "--experimental-vm-modules" in script:
    env["NODE_OPTIONS"] = (env.get("NODE_OPTIONS", "") + " --experimental-vm-modules").strip()
print("Running: " + " ".join(cmd), flush=True)
sys.exit(subprocess.run(cmd, env=env, timeout=1500).returncode)

requirements.text: Build the app with Vite + React + TypeScript and use react-router for routing.
Use plain CSS with a design-token theme defined as CSS custom properties.
Running `npm run build` produces dist/index.html.
The site is static, with no backend and no user accounts.
No analytics and no third-party scripts are included.
No external font CDNs or image CDNs are used; only system font stacks are used.
The brand name shown is "The Bayes Group" and the tagline is "Evidence-driven AI, built for your business."
The colour palette is deep navy (#0B1F3A) and white with a single accent colour, teal #1F8A8A, defined as theme tokens.
The site has generous whitespace and looks like a top-tier professional consulting firm.
